scope: Static source/test review against five retained exact-hash function listings; inspected existing PASS record without rerunning tests. No source edits, target execution, process-environment acquisition, or native API calls.
selected_assembly_verification: All five selected function excerpts independently compared exactly, after trimming surrounding whitespace, with corresponding complete retained listing excerpts.
findings: 06F9E4 includes the final wide NUL in conversion count, including a one-unit empty block; count truncation to low 32 bits and signed allocation-size extension match MOV R9D,EBP and MOVSXD R14,EAX.

06F9E4 preserves acquisition/query/allocation/fill branching: acquisition NULL makes no release call; query zero releases the wide block directly; failed malloc calls free(NULL); failed fill frees its buffer; successful fill calls free(NULL); subsequent wide release order agrees with assembly.

063B54 counts entries not beginning with '=' and allocates count+1 slots of size eight. String copies include each terminating NUL, retain duplicates and entries without '=', and publish each pointer only after successful strcpy_s.

063B54 failed string allocation frees previously published strings and their array before the two observed free(NULL) calls. Nonzero strcpy_s invokes nonreturning Watson before publishing that string or adding cleanup.

063D80 reads successive array slots after freeing the previous entry and frees the pointer array only after its NULL terminator; bounded exhaustion is explicitly unsupported rather than invented original validation.

063A70 checks only current pointer before initialization; success publishes initial then current; failed construction skips both writes and preserves provider mutations. The initializer's extra free(NULL) precedes freeing converted block. Low EAX results and 064054 tail-thunk delegation match assembly.
limits: Review assumes complete stable input spans, correctly sized live provider-owned storage, zero-initialized pointer arrays, and normal provider contracts. Arbitrary alias mutation of input block contents during allocator/copy callbacks is outside the reviewed domain; the reconstruction snapshots a bounded final offset rather than claiming such mutations equivalent.

Bounds/capacity metadata, guards and C++ struct layout are reconstruction choices, not recovered ABI or original validation. Huge-span integer truncation is inspected in source but not dynamically allocated in fixtures.
No native environment, code-page conversion, heap, multibyte initialization, fatal-handler backend, SEH/unwind cleanup or concurrency behavior is established.
Five function entries include one tail thunk. Passing fixture counts do not establish original source identity, runtime equivalence or complete DLL reconstruction.
